nodes.label: Fluid Workflow: Actions on a Change Model. Rationale: implementation is not phase-locked; apply can be invoked anytime and artifact updates are allowed when implementation reveals design issues
nodes.norm_label: fluid workflow: actions on a change model. rationale: implementation is not phase-locked; apply can be invoked anytime and artifact updates are allowed when implementation reveals design issues

nodes.label: Intelligent Merging Principle. Rationale: agent-driven merging allows partial updates because the delta represents intent, not wholesale replacement; enables adding a scenario without copying the entire requirement, unlike programmatic merging
nodes.norm_label: intelligent merging principle. rationale: agent-driven merging allows partial updates because the delta represents intent, not wholesale replacement; enables adding a scenario without copying the entire requirement, unlike programmatic merging

nodes.label: Explore Mode Stance. Rationale: a stance not a workflow - thinking partner mode with no fixed steps; never writes code because exploring and implementing must stay separated; creating OpenSpec artifacts counts as capturing thinking, not implementing
nodes.norm_label: explore mode stance. rationale: a stance not a workflow - thinking partner mode with no fixed steps; never writes code because exploring and implementing must stay separated; creating openspec artifacts counts as capturing thinking, not implementing

nodes.label: Update vs Start Fresh Heuristic. Rationale: if a request changes a change's intent rather than refining it, start a fresh change with /opsx:new instead of updating; update only revises existing planning artifacts and never advances the build frontier
nodes.norm_label: update vs start fresh heuristic. rationale: if a request changes a change's intent rather than refining it, start a fresh change with /opsx:new instead of updating; update only revises existing planning artifacts and never advances the build frontier

nodes.norm_label: next.js version warning. rationale: this next.js version has breaking changes vs training data; agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code and heed deprecation notices

nodes.label: Phone-home Protocol
nodes.rationale: Instances report telemetry every 60s via Bearer-authenticated heartbeats; commands array reserved empty in v0 for forward-compat (restart, update in v0.5+). Heartbeats accumulate as time points, never deduplicated.

nodes.label: POST /api/v0/pair (Pairing Flow)
nodes.rationale: Single-use human-readable 6-8 char code valid 10 min exchanged for a long-lived hashed instance_token; keeps worker onboarding to typing one code in a first-run wizard.

nodes.label: Instance entity
nodes.rationale: instance_token stored hashed (bcrypt/argon2), never plaintext; status online/offline/unpaired computed in query from last_heartbeat_at with 3-min threshold, not stored — v0 accepts polling lag over realtime complexity.

nodes.label: Heartbeat entity
nodes.rationale: raw_payload jsonb column kept for forward compatibility so unknown telemetry fields survive schema evolution.

nodes.label: Magic Link Auth (NextAuth, no password)
nodes.rationale: Passwordless magic link chosen to avoid password management for a tiny v0 user base; operators seeded manually, firm_admins created by operators, workers never log into clawhub — only into clawgents-desktop.

nodes.label: Admin Console (operator + firm screens)
nodes.rationale: 7 functional screens, zero polish — scope deliberately capped for a 2-week v0 demoable for the first in-situ install.

nodes.label: Column-based Multi-tenancy (firm_id)
nodes.rationale: firm_id column on each relevant table judged sufficient for v0 over schema/db-per-tenant; data-leakage risk mitigated by isolation tests and auth middleware checking firm_id on every query.

nodes.label: clawhub-agent (headless phone-home client)
nodes.rationale: Single-file Node 18+ client with no Electron and no npm install so an existing OpenClaw gateway+bridge PC can appear in clawhub without installing full clawgents-desktop; pairs once, persists token at ~/.clawhub-client/config.json (mode 600), heartbeats every 60s with locally-probed bridge/agent state.

nodes.label: Unified Flow: configurator → clawhub → installer → machine
nodes.rationale: Decision (17-jun): reactivate and close gaps rather than rebuild — clawhub already models the whole flow (Firm=license, PairingToken.code=install code, Instance=machine, FirmBaseline=package, StackBundle=installer).
nodes.norm_label: unified flow: configurator → clawhub → installer → machine

nodes.label: clawhub as License Authority
nodes.rationale: Registration validates against Firm (exists + active) in clawhub, NOT against smartbotics; smartbotics is retired from the installer or reduced to only creating the Firm on sale. The installer's validate_license would point to clawhub.

nodes.label: FirmBaseline (configurator package)
nodes.rationale: The configurator wizard package maps onto FirmBaseline: base/openclaw.json = category OPENCLAW_CONFIG, workspaces = WORKSPACE, overlay-config translates to FirmAgentInstall selection or stored as OTHER.

nodes.label: MAC/deviceId capture gap in Instance
nodes.rationale: Additive (non-destructive) migration adding Instance.mac captured during v0/pair to bind a license install to physical hardware.

nodes.label: Supabase Project Paused (blocker)
nodes.rationale: Supabase pjjixcylawrqimtdzjzy paused — without DB clawhub cannot run or be tested; until operator restores it, only design/code, no validation.

nodes.label: Kill-switch (suspend/resume by subscription)
nodes.rationale: The cut is a reversible 'real suspended mode' (gate on tasks/chat) that does not kill processes (JJ's decision); heartbeat stays HTTP 200 while suspended so the instance keeps being monitored; reuses existing pairing, heartbeat, command auth and admin endpoints.

nodes.label: Bridge Suspension Gate (402 subscription_suspended)
nodes.rationale: Persistent file flag (<BRIDGE_DATA_DIR>/.suspended) survives restarts; task/chat creation returns 402 subscription_suspended before dispatch; health endpoint exposes suspended state for a web banner.

nodes.label: Dispatcher firm_status → bridge suspend/resume translation
nodes.rationale: The client dispatcher reads firm_status from each heartbeat response and idempotently POSTs /api/admin/suspend or /api/admin/resume to the local bridge, keeping local state to avoid repeats.

nodes.label: Role Model (OPERATOR, EMPRESA, COMERCIAL, FIRM_ADMIN)
nodes.rationale: Each role gets its own layout and protected routes via requireXxx() guards in Server Components; only pre-registered User emails can log in.

nodes.label: Dev Auth Bypass (DEV_AUTH_ENABLED)
nodes.rationale: Role-button login on /login without password or real email speeds up local development; must be removed from production .env.

nodes.label: Vista Comercial (/sales prospect pipeline)
nodes.rationale: 5-stage visual pipeline (Nuevo → Contactado → Visitó landing → En negociación → Compra) with per-row quick send of the active campaign via email/SMS carrying a personalized tracking link.

nodes.label: Tracking Token (?t=TOKEN attribution)
nodes.rationale: Each sent link carries a per-prospect trackingToken registered on visit (LandingVisit) and on purchase (Purchase), enabling automatic sale attribution to the correct comercial.

nodes.label: End-to-end Sale Flow (prospect → Stripe → Firm)
nodes.rationale: Step 7b pending: after creating the FIRM_ADMIN user the buyer should be redirected or emailed access to the AI-Office installer; installer route undefined so the Edge Function hook is deferred.

nodes.label: Stripe Webhook Edge Function (Supabase/Deno)
nodes.rationale: On checkout.session.completed it creates the Firm, creates the FIRM_ADMIN user, records the Purchase, marks the Prospect PURCHASED and computes the commission; the clawhub schema is exposed in the Supabase API precisely so this Edge Function can reach it.

nodes.label: openclaw-configurator Review Notes
nodes.rationale: Pending review items: only the selected provider should be emitted by the configurator (same for clawhub) and Models section (MiniMax + Ollama) needs review in models and agents.

nodes.label: openclaw.json Config Template (MiniMax/Ollama stack)
nodes.rationale: Reference gateway config: token-auth local gateway, MiniMax-M3 primary with MiniMax-M2.7/ollama fallbacks, plugin allow/deny lists (denies openai/anthropic/google etc. providers), skills whitelist, secrets resolved via bridge_tokens exec resolver, placeholders __GATEWAY_TOKEN__/__STACK_ROOT__/__NODE_BIN__ filled at provision time.

nodes.label: Bundle Auto-registration Pipeline (tag → release → register)
nodes.rationale: Pushing a v* tag packs the repo (tar.gz or .exe), creates a GitHub Release, and self-registers the artifact in clawhub with sha256+url+sizeBytes; the bundle then appears in /operator/stack and the operator only pins it to firms — removing manual upload steps from release flow.

nodes.label: OPERATOR_API_KEY (M2M auth for bundle registration)
nodes.rationale: Shared secret (openssl rand -hex 32) configured both as GitHub secret CLAWHUB_API_KEY and Vercel env var OPERATOR_API_KEY, used as Bearer token for machine-to-machine bundle registration.

nodes.label: release-installer.yml (kind=INSTALLER, .exe)
nodes.rationale: Runs on windows-latest because electron-builder NSIS only builds on Windows; code-signing (CSC_LINK/CSC_KEY_PASSWORD) deferred until an OV cert exists.
